statements.t: In addition to traditional commercial banking products, the Company offers: corporate cash management and retail banking services; tailored financial solutions for government entities, municipalities, and public institutions; specialized services to facilitate secure and efficient real estate transactions and tax-deferred exchanges for title and escrow and Section 1031 exchanges; and EB-5 Program escrow accounts…
Management believes that the ACL for loans and loan commitments is adequate to cover expected credit losses over the life of the loan portfolio.

Prior to the third quarter of 2026, the Company utilized lifetime loss rate models to calculate the expected losses over the life of the loan based on exposure at default loan attributes, and reasonable and supportable economic forecasts.

The Company determined that the DCF methodology provides a more granular and enhanced measurement framework through its use of individual loan characteristics, contractual cash flows, prepayment assumptions, expected loss expectations, and timing of expected cash flows into the ACL estimate.
As part of the implementation the Company updated its loan segmentation, peer data methodology, economic forecast assumptions and certain model inputs, including prepayment assumptions.
The Company uses a four-quarter reasonable and supportable forecast period followed by a four-quarter straight-line reversion to the long-term average of the applicable economic variable.

To illustrate the sensitivity of the ACL to changes in the economic forecast, the Company increased forecasted unemployment by 10% over the reasonable and supportable forecast period while holding all other model assumptions constant.

This hypothetical analysis is intended solely to illustrate the impact of a change in forecasted unemployment at a point in time and does not reflect management's expectations regarding future economic conditions or the full nature and extent of potential future changes in the ACL.

The Company regularly reviews the need to adjust investments in liquid assets based upon its assessment of: (1) expected loan demand, (2) expected deposit flows, (3) yields available on interest-earning deposits and securities, and (4) the objectives of its asset/liability program.

In the event loan demand were to increase faster than expected, or any other unforeseen demand or commitment were to occur, the Company could access its borrowing capacity with the FHLB or obtain additional funds through alternative funding sources, including the brokered deposit market.
The Company and the Bank manage their capital to comply with their internal planning targets and regulatory capital standards administered by federal banking agencies.

estimates.name: Allowance for Credit Losses
estimates.t: Although management evaluates available information to determine the adequacy of the ACL, the level of allowance is an estimate which is subject to significant judgment and short-term change.
estimates.effect: The effect of this change in accounting estimate for the three months ended March 31, 2026, was a net decrease in the provision for credit losses of $6.4 million, which is $4.6 million, net of tax, or $0.43 per basic earnings per share and $0.42 per dilutive earnings per share.

estimates.name: Discussion of Financial Condition
estimates.t: The Company had total assets of $9.5 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $1.2 billion, or 14.7%, from December 31, 2025.

estimates.name: Investments
estimates.t: Total securities were $1.5 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $546.8 million or 58.1%, from December 31, 2025.

estimates.name: Loans
estimates.t: Total loans, net of deferred fees and unamortized costs, were $7.5 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $723.6 million, or 10.6%, from December 31, 2025.

estimates.name: ​
estimates.t: As of September 30, 2026, total loans consisted primarily of CRE loans and C&I loans.

estimates.name: ​ — Asset Quality
estimates.t: As the Company continues to work diligently toward the resolution of the credits that make up its nonperforming loan portfolio, non-performing loans decreased to $71.7 million at September 30, 2026 compared to $86.9 million at December 31, 2025.

estimates.name: ​ — Allowance for Credit Losses – Loans and Loan Commitments
estimates.t: The $32.9 million decrease in the ACL primarily reflects enhancements made to the Bank’s allowance for credit loss estimation process in the first quarter of 2026, as well as the charge-off of the aforementioned previously reserved CRE loan relationship, partially offset by loan growth.

estimates.name: Deposits
estimates.t: Total deposits were $8.3 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $943.4 million, or 12.8%, from December 31, 2025.

estimates.name: ​ — ​ — ​
estimates.t: At September 30, 2026, the aggregate estimated amount of FDIC uninsured deposits was $2.4 billion, and the aggregate estimated amount of uninsured time deposits was $46.4 million.

estimates.name: ​ — Borrowings
estimates.t: To support the balance sheet, the Company may at times utilize FHLB advances or other funding sources.

estimates.name: Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income
estimates.t: Accumulated other comprehensive loss, net of tax, was $54.6 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $14.9 million from December 31, 2025.
